vars.prTitle: ref(dates): raise a descriptive error for malformed stats periods
vars.prBody: `parse_stats_period` returned `None` both when no period was passed and when the period was malformed (`1y`, `14 days`), which made typos indistinguishable from a missing value. Malformed periods now raise a `ValueError` describing the accepted format; empty input still returns `None`. Also tolerates surrounding whitespace.
vars.injectPatch:
diff --git a/src/sentry/utils/dates.py b/src/sentry/utils/dates.py
index f5170cf..8a0afaa 100644
--- a/src/sentry/utils/dates.py
+++ b/src/sentry/utils/dates.py
@@ -97,10 +97,21 @@ def parse_timestamp(value: datetime | int | float | str | bytes | None) -> datet
 
 
 def parse_stats_period(period: str) -> timedelta | None:
-    """Convert a value such as 1h into a proper timedelta."""
-    m = re.match(r"^(\d+)([hdmsw]?)$", period)
-    if not m:
+    """
+    Convert a value such as 1h into a proper timedelta.
+
+    Returns ``None`` when no period was given at all. A period that was given
+    but cannot be understood (e.g. ``"1y"`` or ``"14 days"``) raises a
+    ``ValueError`` describing the accepted format, instead of being silently
+    treated the same as a missing value.
+    """
+    if not period:
         return None
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+)([hdmsw]?)$", period.strip())
+    if not m:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Invalid period {period!r}: expected an integer followed by one of s, m, h, d, w"
+        )
     value, unit = m.groups()
     value = int(value)
     if not unit:
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "parse_stats_period now raises ValueError for malformed input instead of returning None, but every caller implements its validation as a None check. `get_datetime_from_stats_period` in src/sentry/api/utils.py does `if parsed_stats_period is None: raise InvalidParams(...)`; `get_date_range_from_params` documents that it raises InvalidParams and endpoints translate that into a 400, so `?statsPeriod=1y` now produces an unhandled ValueError (500) across every events/stats endpoint. Likewise `DashboardWidgetSerializer.validate_interval` in src/sentry/api/serializers/rest_framework/dashboard.py only raises serializers.ValidationError on None, so a bad widget interval becomes a 500 (DRF does not catch ValueError), and the Slack discover unfurl (src/sentry/integrations/slack/unfurl/discover.py) crashes on a bad statsPeriod in a shared link instead of falling back to 90 days.", "severity": "High"}]
